As someone who did MKT412, MKT465, MKT330 and MKT382, I would recommend you to take courses based on what you will be learning rather than just getting an A/A- in the course. Of course grades are important but so is learning.
MKT412 (ZTK) I found this course pretty easy. It is mostly about making processes and designing the services of a business. So it is more about the backend part of a business and its marketing. Really enjoyed my time in this course with ZTK ma'am. Totally worth doing the course. Easy to get a good grade, ngl.
MKT465 (ZTK) This course was quite interesting as it required creativity (more than other MKT courses) in the exams and the main group project a lot. If you think that you are creative enough then it's actually a pretty good course to do so, under ZTK ma'am. There's SeH Ma'am as well. You can take her section too. It's a bit competitive to get a good grade in this course but nothing impossible at all.
MKT330 (Ehn) This course is a lot different from others (Well, every course is different) but there are a couple of contents you might find similar to the previous courses you have done. But man oh man! Ehn Sir literally teaches you how to run ads and campaigns, even how to do A/B testing as well, practically. It might be a bit competitive to get a good grade in this course if you are taking Ehn Sir's section but yeah you gotta give in a lot of effort.
Now rest is up to you. Choose and decide wisely!

Last semester I took MKT330 as my free elective and chose NYM because of the overwhelming hype—“she’s the best,” “curve queen,” all that. But attending her classes turned out to be nothing short of a nightmare. After MaNA, she’s honestly one of the pettiest faculty at NSU.
She was blatantly biased toward students who had already taken MKT220 with her, especially the guys. Even the CR was from her previous course. Throughout the semester, I felt constantly targeted. I already struggle with severe anxiety, and her behavior only made it worse. During Mid 1, while I was writing my exam, she suddenly came up, checked my name, and walked away—no explanation. During our presentation, she straight-up ignored my part.
She also holds these so-called one-to-one sessions with students, but when my turn came, she was scrolling on her phone instead of listening.
In short: if you’re good at buttering up professors, you’ll thrive with her and probably get more than you deserve. If not, save yourself the mental exhaustion and just go with Ehn.
